title: Etale sections lift modulo the radical of a henselian ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Put $J=\sqrt I=\{a\in A:\exists n>0,\ a^n\in I\}$. Let $A\to B$ be a ring map such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For every $A$-algebra homomorphism $\bar\sigma:B\to A/J$ there exists an $A$-algebra homomorphism $\sigma:B\to A$ whose composite with $A\to A/J$ is $\bar\sigma$.

proof.text: If $A=0$, its unital algebra $B$ is also the zero ring, and the unique map $B\to A$ has the required reduction. Hence assume $A\ne0$.

proof.text: We first prove that $(A,J)$ is henselian. For any finite $A$-algebra $C$, the kernel $K$ of $C/IC\to C/JC$ consists of nilpotent elements. Indeed, a representative in $JC$ is a finite sum $\sum_{i=1}^m a_i c_i$ with $a_i\in J$; choose $n_i>0$ with $a_i^{n_i}\in I$. For $m>0$, expanding its $N$th power, where $N=1+\sum_i(n_i-1)$, shows that every term contains some $a_i^{n_i}$, so the power belongs to $IC$. The empty sum is zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotents-locally-nilpotent] to $C/IC$ and $K$: $C/IC\to C/JC$ induces a bijection on idempotents. Henselianity of $(A,I)$ gives a bijection on idempotents for $C\to C/IC$. Composing these bijections gives the defining condition of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] for $(A,J)$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion] for $(A,J)$, $J$ lies in the Jacobson radical and coprime monic factorizations lift modulo $J$. For $f(T)=T^n(T-1)+\sum_{i=0}^n a_iT^i$ with $n\ge1$ and $a_i\in J$, the factors $T^n$ and $T-1$ of its reduction are coprime: $T^n-(T-1)(1+T+\cdots+T^{n-1})=1$. Lift them to monic $g,h$ with $f=gh$ and $\bar h=T-1$. Since $A\ne0$ and $J$ lies in the Jacobson radical, $A/J\ne0$; reduction preserves the degree of a monic polynomial. Thus $h$ has degree one, say $h=T-\alpha$, and $\bar h=T-1$ gives $\alpha-1\in J$. Evaluating $f=gh$ at $\alpha$ gives $f(\alpha)=0$. This proves precisely Gabber's root condition for $J$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-gabber-root-criterion-etale-section-lifting] with ideal $J$, etale algebra $B$, and the given $\bar\sigma:B\to A/J$. The preceding step verifies both its Jacobson-radical and polynomial-root hypotheses. It gives an $A$-algebra map $\sigma:B\to A$ whose composite with $A\to A/J$ is exactly $\bar\sigma$, as required.
